text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure is widely known as a "silent killer" because it typically causes no warning signs or symptoms at all.
snippet_highlighted_words: no warning signs or symptoms at all

text_blocks.snippet: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine. However, a sudden spike or severely elevated levels can occasionally lead to subtle signs that are easy to overlook:

list.snippet: Early-morning headaches: A dull, persistent ache at the back of the head upon waking.
Dizziness or lightheadedness: A brief woozy feeling caused by changes in blood flow.
Blurred vision: Strain or changes in vision due to delicate eye vessel stress.
Shortness of breath: Getting winded easily during light physical exertion.
Pounding sensation: A rhythmic thumping felt in the ears, neck, or chest.

text_blocks.snippet: Readings exceeding 180/120 mm Hg constitute a medical emergency, as detailed by the American Heart Association. Seek immediate emergency care by calling 911 if a high reading is accompanied by:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Your most recent blood pressure reading (if you have one)
Whether you are experiencing any specific symptoms right now
